title: Migrate Redis client to async-native API and remove blocking hooks
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Background:
Our current Redis integration for worker pipelines uses a hybrid sync/async client shim that relies on short-lived blocking hooks to integrate with legacy delivery/retry code paths. Over time this pattern has introduced latency spikes under tail load, complicated backpressure reasoning, and made it difficult to adopt the newer Netty-based async client we need for the planned CPU and connection pool optimizations.

Goal:
- Replace the blocking shim with the upstream async-native Redis client across the ingest + retry + lease reconciliation paths.
- Remove places where threads are parked waiting on blocking IO and instead use fully async flows (CompletableFuture/Flux/Task depending on service language bindings).
- Reduce tail latency, reduce thread pool pressure, and simplify retry semantics by making acknowledgement/deferred-ack flows event-driven instead of blocking.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope: consumer ingress, deferred-ack/visibility, lease renewals, retry coordinator, and optimistic-prefetch logic touched by blocking calls.
- Non-goal: re-architecting the partitioning/sharding strategy or changing message format. Those are separate tickets.

Acceptance criteria:
- No remaining usages of BlockingRedisClient.* APIs in the pipeline services (verified via code scan).
- End-to-end p95 message delivery latency improved by >= 15% under the 99th percentile producer load in benchmark harness.
- CPU and thread count under sustained load reduced by at least 20% compared to baseline (benchmark run).
- No increase in message duplication or ordering regressions; integration test suite for dedupe and ordering passes.
- All affected services can be toggled between old and new client via a feature flag for staged rollout.

Implementation plan:
1) Audit: annotate and list all callsites that invoke blocking Redis calls (ingest, retry coordinator, lease service, visibility processor). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/redis-blocking-audit
2) Create async adapter library that exposes the thin compatibility layer used by pipeline code and wraps the new async client with safe timeout and retry policies. This adapter must be suitable for use in both JVM and native pipelines.
3) Incrementally replace callsites starting with low-risk components: lease renewals -> deferred-ack -> retry coordinator -> ingress. Each replacement goes through an internal benchmark harness.
4) Add feature flag and an opt-in rollout path (gateway config + per-cluster toggle) so we can route a small percentage of traffic to the async path and observe differences.
5) Run a staged canary in staging and then in a single low-traffic region during off-peak hours. Monitor key SLOs and rollback on error.

Testing & Benchmarks:
- Create benchmark harness that simulates producer spikes and long-tail meshes; collect p50/p95/p99 latency, consumer throughput, thread count, GC time, and connection pool metrics.
- Add integration tests that simulate connection timeout, partial failures, and lease contention to assert no message loss or deadlocks.
- Add chaos test that kills worker threads and verifies system recovers without stuck leases.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: subtle ordering/visibility regressions when switching to async flows. Mitigation: expanded integration tests with deterministic message stamps and a verification pass that runs against canary traffic.
- Risk: new client has slightly different connection semantics causing transient errors under very high fanout. Mitigation: add circuit-breaker and backoff wrappers to the adapter and run soak tests in staging at 2x traffic.
- Risk: library upgrade surfaces transitive dependency conflicts. Mitigation: isolate change in a small adapter module and coordinate with infra dependency upgrade window; keep the old client as a compile-time optional dependency during migration.

Observability changes:
- Add metric: redis_async_inflight_commands gauge by service + shard.
- Add histogram: redis_async_command_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99 buckets).
- Add rollup dashboard comparing blocking vs async path (latency, threads, connection pool saturation).

Rollout checklist:
- [ ] Adapter module PR merged and published to internal repo.
- [ ] Unit + integration tests green.
- [ ] Benchmark showing improvement or parity.
- [ ] Feature flag wired and verified in staging.
- [ ] Canary deploy to single region with 5% traffic.
- [ ] Monitor for 48 hours, then increase to 25%.
- [ ] Full migration and removal of old shim code + cleanup PR.

Notes and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/async-redis-migration
- Initial benchmark results (baseline): https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/redis/baseline-2026-01-15
- Related tickets: ENG-316271 (resumable-offset-checkpoints), ENG-527301 (ingress decompose).
